title: Storm Light on the Divide
story: Snow on the peaks, storm cloud stacking up behind them, and a single road threading through the middle of it all. The kind of country that makes you feel appropriately small.

title: Mirror Mirror
location: Lake Matheson, Fox Glacier, New Zealand
story: This is one of those places that no words can describe. On a calm morning with the lake perfectly reflecting the mountains, it is blissful.

title: The Valley That Feels Like Legend
story: A braided river, a lone conical peak, and nothing else for miles — this stretch of high country has a way of looking like it belongs in someone else's story.

title: Guardians of the Cove
story: A sea stack standing sentry over turquoise water and pale cliffs — one of the most photographed coves in the country, and still worth the walk in. I shot two versions of the same shot; this is the short exposure, and the other is a long exposure using a 10-stop ND filter.

title: Mt Doom in winter
story: Fresh snow on Mt Ngaruhoe, a perfectly symmetrical volcano, with nothing but frozen scoria in every direction. It's easy to see why this mountain has played bigger roles than itself.

title: Where the Glacier Ends
location: Hooker Valley, Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, New Zealand
story: A milky glacial lake sitting at the foot of Mt Sefton, fed by ice that's been retreating for decades. Beautiful and quietly sobering at the same time.

title: Ice Blue, Sky Blue
location: Hooker Valley, Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, New Zealand
story: Same valley, same lake, a different hour — the kind of blue that only glacial silt can make.

title: The Road to Aoraki
location: Lake Pukaki, Mackenzie Basin, New Zealand
story: Impossibly turquoise water leads the eye straight to the country's tallest peak — one of the classic New Zealand views, and it never quite stops being one.

title: Pukaki at Dusk
location: Lake Pukaki, Mackenzie Basin, New Zealand
story: The colour drains out of the sky in slow motion here — pink fading to blue, the mountains going from gold to grey to silhouette.

title: Golden Shoreline
story: A curved gravel bay catching the last of the day's light, mountains standing quietly along the far shore.

title: Wind Over the Paddocks
location: Duder Regional Park, Hauraki Gulf coastline, New Zealand
story: Green farmland rolling down to the water, wisps of high cloud streaking overhead — a working landscape that happens to be beautiful too.

title: Taranaki, Twice
story: On a still day, the lake gives you the mountain twice over — once in the sky, once in the water, bush framing it both ways. Count yourself lucky to see the mountain; it is quite often covered in cloud.

title: That Tree, Alone
story: One willow, one lake, a thousand photographs before this one — and it still holds up in black and white, still and solitary against the water.

title: Sunburst at Cathedral Cove
story: The sun breaks right over the sea stack, the wet sand throwing the whole scene back at itself.

title: Gannet
story: The gannet colony at Muriwai is a popular spot to visit for Aucklanders.

title: The Road to the Mountain
location: Desert Road, Central Plateau, New Zealand
story: A ribbon of road pointed straight at a snow-capped volcano — one of the great drives, best seen right as dawn breaks.

title: Two Giants at Twilight
location: Desert Road, Central Plateau, New Zealand
story: Ruapehu on one side, Ngauruhoe on the other, and the whole plateau caught in that brief window between dark and day.

title: First Light on Ruapehu
story: The very first colour of the day landing on the summit, everything below it still in shadow.

title: Alpenglow on the Volcano
story: That brief pink flush of alpenglow across the cone, the road curving away toward it like an invitation.

title: Still Water, Otago
story: Jagged peaks laid flat on glassy water, a quiet grassy point reaching out into the lake — the kind of scene that makes you stop talking.

title: Black Sand, Green Rock
story: Volcanic sand, algae-slicked rocks, and a towering eroded cliff — the raw, unpolished side of Auckland's coastline.

title: Through the Sea Cave
location: Bethells Beach, Auckland's west coast, New Zealand
story: A cave mouth framing a black-sand beach and a distant rock stack — the kind of spot you only find by wandering further than you planned to.

title: Point England Reserve
location: Point England Reserve, Auckland, New Zealand

title: Sunrise on Desert Road
location: Desert Road, Central Plateau, New Zealand
story: I had been planning to shoot this location for many years, but things just never quite lined up for me. The location is on Desert Road (State Highway 1); it is far enough away from home that I couldn't just drive there for a sunrise. I had a week off work, so I decided I would stay overnight in Ohakune and then hope that the conditions would be good for a sunrise shot of the volcanoes of Tongariro National Park. It turned out the conditions were fantastic except for the stiff, cold southerly that seemed to have one purpose: to freeze anything in its path to death. My fingers were numb after shooting this. I struggled to keep the camera stable, especially because I was shooting with a relatively long focal length. The result turned out decent despite the hostile conditions.

title: The Bridge Over the Falls
story: A footbridge crossing directly over the lip of a bush waterfall — an unusual vantage that makes the falls feel almost incidental to the walk.

title: Westhaven at Rest
story: Before the city properly wakes, the marina is just masts and stillness — hundreds of boats waiting, the Sky Tower keeping watch in the distance.

title: The Long Walk Out
story: A concrete ramp running straight out into the harbour, one person sitting at the end of it, the whole city glowing pink and distant. There's a particular kind of loneliness that only shows up at dusk.

title: Steel Against the Dark
story: Stripped of colour, the bridge becomes pure structure — arcs of light holding up the night, the city glinting faintly through its ribs.

title: Cyril Bassett VC Lookout
story: This location has become one of my favourite vantage points of the city.

title: First One After Lockdown
story: After spending what seemed like an eternity in lockdown during the COVID-19 pandemic, I was desperate to get out with my camera. This was the result.

title: Adelaide, Blue Hour
story: The Torrens goes still and mirror-flat right as the convention centre lights click on — that narrow window where the sky is still blue but the city already looks like nightfall.

title: Adelaide Cityscape
story: Caught this fountain right at blue hour, a few minutes after the Christmas lights kicked on across the square.

title: City Lights, Still Water
story: The Sky Tower catches the last colour in the sky while the harbour holds it all in reflection, twice over.

title: The Beehive in Bloom
story: A pōhutukawa in full red flower stands guard over the seat of government — an unexpectedly soft frame for one of the country's most recognisable buildings.

title: Rush Hour, Slow Water
story: Traffic streaks past in a blur of light while, just metres away, a thousand yacht masts don't move at all. Two speeds of the same evening.

title: Boats Beneath the Bridge
story: Small yachts at anchor, dwarfed by the bridge's long red glow — a quiet foreground for something this big.

title: Sky Tower hi res in sunset light
Underneath
story: Looking straight up into the trusswork as the lights come on, the bridge stops being a way to cross the harbour and becomes architecture in its own right.

title: Moonrise Over the Marina
story: A full moon hangs over the skyline while the motorway below streaks red and white — one slow light in the sky, thousands of fast ones on the ground.

title: A Forest of Masts
story: Hundreds of bare masts stand black against a bruised purple sky, the city just a smudge of light behind them.

title: Flying Colours
story: Looking up through the trees as traffic streams beneath the flags — an angle that makes even a daily commute look like an occasion.

title: Last Light on the Bridge
story: The last warm colour of the day catches the underside of the arch, the Sky Tower glowing faintly through the gap.

title: The Quiet Memorial
location: MJ Savage Memorial Park, Auckland, New Zealand
story: An obelisk and a formal garden, empty and still at dusk — the kind of place that asks you to slow down without saying why.

title: Vertical City
story: Traffic drags long streaks of colour down the street while the Sky Tower stands perfectly still above it, unbothered by the rush below.

title: Streets of Light
story: The same tower, a different night — this time the city exhales in ribbons of red and gold, funnelled straight downhill.

title: Gathering Clouds Over the City
story: A heavy sky pressing down on the skyline, the water gone flat and grey beneath it — the calm that sits just before weather changes.

title: Evening Commute
story: The marina settles into blue-hour quiet while the motorway keeps moving — everyone else's evening still underway.

title: Icy Tasman Lake
location: Tasman Glacier, Aoraki/Mt Cook National Park
story: I have a few images from this spot. I love how, on this day, the glacial lake is filled with icebergs and the late afternoon light is kissing the peaks.

title: The Whale-Bone Bridge

title: Sky on Fire
story: A sunrise that turns the whole sky the colour of embers, rocks and a lone pōhutukawa silhouetted against it.

title: The Jetty Between Two Bays
story: A single jetty splitting two curved beaches, a small boat moored alongside — the kind of view that makes you want to just sit at the end of it.

title: Grass, Rock, and a Falling Sun
story: Windswept grass in the foreground, an offshore rock catching the day's last light — a coastline that always looks like it's in a mood.

title: Sunset in the Cove
location: Oneroa Bay Beach (Long Bay), Russell, New Zealand
story: A cove closed in on both sides by dark headlands, the sky doing all the work in gold and violet.

title: Where the Cliffs Meet the Tide
location: Oneroa Bay Beach (Long Bay), Russell, New Zealand
story: The same bay, the tide a little further in, rock stacks catching the last warm light before the colour goes out of the sky entirely.

title: The Hidden Lagoon
location: Te Arai Beach, Auckland, New Zealand
story: A pocket of impossibly clear water tucked behind a rocky headland — the sort of spot that only reveals itself once you've climbed over the hill to look.

title: Layers of Light
story: Cliffs stacked in warm gold, the coastline curving away into haze — golden hour doing exactly what it does best.

title: Storm's Edge
story: Heavy cloud breaking just enough to let the sun through in hard shafts of light over a wild, wind-whipped sea.

title: The River's Fury
story: White water churning over volcanic rock, a modest drop doing its best impression of something much bigger.

title: Cascade Over the Dome
story: Water fans out over a mossy rock dome in dozens of separate threads, tree ferns crowding in on every side.

title: Veils of White
story: The same cascade, pulled back a little wider — water falling like a curtain rather than a single stream.

title: Nikau and Water
location: Karekare, Waitākere Ranges, Auckland, New Zealand
story: A tiered waterfall dropping into a turquoise pool, nikau palms leaning in as if they came just to watch.

title: Karekare Falls
location: Karekare, Waitākere Ranges, Auckland, New Zealand

title: The Long Fall
story: A single unbroken drop from a hanging cliff, the base lost in its own mist by the time the water gets there.

title: Taranaki Falls in Winter
story: The falls still running hard even with snow banked up along the pool's edge — proof that winter here is more bark than bite.

title: The Colour of Huka
story: That impossible turquoise isn't a filter — it's just how much water the Waikato River is forcing through a gap this narrow.

title: Green Cathedral
story: Moss thick enough to look upholstered, a narrow fall of water cutting straight through the middle of it.

title: Wide and Wild
location: Karekare, Waitākere Ranges, Auckland, New Zealand
story: A broad curtain of falling water fanning into a dark, still pool — more volume than height, and all the more dramatic for it.

title: The Falls, Standing Tall
location: Taranaki Falls, Tongariro National Park, New Zealand
story: The full drop in one vertical frame, snow still lingering at the base while the water keeps working.

title: Framed by the Forest
location: Karekare, Waitākere Ranges, Auckland, New Zealand
story: An overhanging branch and a nikau palm doing the framing this time — the same falls, seen the way you'd actually stumble on them.

title: Fire Written in the Air
story: Spinning fire traced into a long exposure until it stops looking like poi and starts looking like something drawn by hand.

title: Sparks and Motion
story: A single frame holding several seconds of movement — fire flung, caught, and flung again.

title: Rings of Flame
story: Two overlapping circles of fire, traced so cleanly they could almost be a logo rather than a performance.

title: Flight Paths
story: Dozens of takeoffs stacked into one exposure until the night sky looks strung with wire.

title: Departures
story: Aircraft banking away from the runway, their trails curling back over the city they just left.

title: Crossing in the Dark
story: A long, low bridge traced entirely in the tail-lights of everyone crossing it after dark.

title: Night Traffic, Ancient Mountain
location: Desert Road, Central Plateau, New Zealand
story: Car lights streak past in red and gold while an eleven-thousand-year-old volcano looks on, entirely unmoved.

title: Playing with fire
story: Spinning steel wool at an Auckland Beach at sunrise.

title: City Lights
story: Stacked long-exposure light trails of the ferries coming in and out of the ferry terminal in Auckland.

title: Quiet Corner of the Park
story: Autumn leaves scattered across open grass, mature trees casting long afternoon shade — an ordinary park moment that's easy to walk straight past.

title: Dahlias in Bloom
story: A tangle of yellow, orange and pink dahlias, the kind of close-up burst of colour that's a deliberate change of pace from wide-open landscapes.
